newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican business doubts govt with economic plan.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican business doubts govt with economic plan.

text.p: South African business told Deputy-President Thabo Mbeki on Tuesday it was uncertain about government's commitment and ability to implement the macro-economic strategy, state television reported.

At a meeting with Mbeki in Pretoria, the South African Chamber of Commerce called on government to step up its efforts to implement Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's new economic plan in the face of declining economic growth since mid-1996, increased inflation and the weakening rand.
Mbeki assured the delegation that government was keen to work with business in boosting the economy.

"Both sides, government and business...have over the months come to understand each other's concerns and interests," Mbeki told television news after the meeting, called by the chamber to drive home its message of boosting economic growth.

Meanwhile in Johannesburg, the Council of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) called for a rethink of the macro-economic plan and warned that the political alliance between itself, the African National Congress (ANC) and the South African Communist Party was teetering.

Cosatu general secretary Sam Shilowa said one way of reviving the tripartite alliance -- which played a big role to secure an ANC majority in the 1994 elections -- was to resuscitate the Reconstruction and Development Programme (RDP).
